aquaponics_coupled_pH_scoring.applies_to: coupled aquaponics loops only; hydroponic scoring keeps preferred_pH / tolerated_pH above
basis: Lower edges from the hydroponic evidence: preferred 5.8, tolerated 5.5 (CEA Herbs factsheet; peer-reviewed hydroponic basil study).

Upper edge 7.6 is the highest pH observed in the UVI aquaponic basil trials (Rakocy et al. 2004, Table 2: 7.4 mean, 7.0 to 7.6 batch; 7.1 mean, 6.9 to 7.3 staggered), where basil yields stayed high with Ca, K and Fe supplementation.
assumptions: pH 6.2 to 6.9 is treated as preferred because it lies between two evidenced good-growth bands; it was not directly observed in either source.
No evidence above pH 7.6, so the score drops to zero there. This is an evidence boundary, not an observed failure.
High-pH Fe deficiency risk above 6.5 (hydroponic note) is assumed managed by supplementation, as at UVI; supplementation is not modelled.
aquaponics_coupled_pH_scoring.evidence_policy: Trusted Source Map and Source Trust Policy for Aquaponics Layer 1: source levels E5-E0, confidence high/medium/low rule

lower_edges_5.5_5.8.source_level: E4 (CEA Herbs factsheet) and E3 (hydroponic basil study)
lower_edges_5.5_5.8.confidence_reason: Same values already in canon as hydroponic ranges; reused for the low end.

upper_edge_7.6.source_level: E3 (Rakocy et al. 2004, Acta Horticulturae) / E4 (UVI)
upper_edge_7.6.confidence_reason: Observed operating pH at a high-yield trial; one site only. It shows basil does well up to 7.6, not that it fails above.

preferred_band_6.2_to_6.9.confidence_reason: Agent inference between two evidenced bands; not observed. Needs Ajit's review.

approval.scope: coupled-aquaponics basil pH scoring: evidenced edges (preferred 5.8, tolerated 5.5, upper 7.6) accepted; the 6.2 to 6.9 preferred band stays a low-confidence assumption
approval.record: Approval Batch 001, approved as recommended (thread message 2026-11-25 23:56 Europe/Amsterdam)

high_pH_nutrient_lockout_notes: At pH above about 6.5, basil risk increases for iron deficiency and interveinal chlorosis.
Corrective action thresholds are suggested around pH 6.2 to 6.4 on the high side.
Aquaponics can still operate near neutral pH, but supplementation with Ca, K, and Fe may be needed.
low_pH_sensitivity_notes: Below about pH 5.8, basil risk increases for iron and manganese toxicity symptoms.
Corrective action thresholds are suggested around 5.5 to 5.7 on the low side.

shoot_dry_matter_fraction.basis: Derived from Table 1 shoot fresh and dry mass: greenhouse 158/1417 g and 165/1452 g (11.2 to 11.4 percent); indoors 31/344 and 32/359 g (about 9.0 percent). Default is the greenhouse value, closest to warm UVI conditions (29/24 C day/night).
shoot_dry_matter_fraction.source: Solis-Toapanta, Fisher, Gomez 2020, 'Growth Rate and Nutrient Uptake of Basil in Small-scale Hydroponics', HortScience, doi 10.21273/HORTSCI14727-19

evidence_assessment.context_completeness: partial (small DWC, Florida greenhouse, Genovese Compact)
evidence_assessment.confidence_reason: Printed values from a peer-reviewed study with two runs; the fraction is our arithmetic, not stated by the authors.

tissue_n_fraction_of_dry_mass.basis: Default is the low end of the 4 to 6 percent survey sufficiency range the paper cites. Greenhouse plants measured 2.2 to 2.9 percent, which the authors say was below that range because N supply limited growth; UVI basil had ample nitrate (about 42 mg/L), so the sufficiency range fits better.
tissue_n_fraction_of_dry_mass.source: Solis-Toapanta, Fisher, Gomez 2020, 'Growth Rate and Nutrient Uptake of Basil in Small-scale Hydroponics', HortScience, doi 10.21273/HORTSCI14727-19
tissue_n_fraction_of_dry_mass.quote: final tissue N concentration was below the survey range

evidence_assessment.directness: direct_number (Table 4 and the cited survey range)
evidence_assessment.confidence_reason: Peer-reviewed, printed values. Measured values vary 2.2 to 6.2 percent with conditions, so the default carries real uncertainty; the survey's original source was not checked.

shoot_n_uptake_model.scope: Shoot uptake only. Roots and the stem left after cutting are not included (the study measured shoots only), so uptake is likely understated.
shoot_n_uptake_model.evidence_policy: Trusted Source Map and Source Trust Policy for Aquaponics Layer 1: source levels E5-E0, confidence high/medium/low rule

growth_notes: Aquaponic basil yield anchor: about 2.0 kg/m2 in batch production and about 1.8 kg/m2 in staggered production under UVI commercial-scale conditions.
Cultivar selection affects basil yield more than the difference between common hydroponic systems such as NFT versus DFT.
Preferred air temperature is about 26.0 to 27.5 C for strong basil growth.
Preferred root-zone or nutrient solution temperature is about 27.5 C for greater growth for most cultivars.
Hydroponic nutrient anchor: about 100 to 150 ppm N with preferred EC about 0.5 to 1.5 mS/cm.
stress_notes: Basil is chilling sensitive: temperatures below about 10 C can cause chilling injury and marketability loss, with severe injury at 5 C or below.
Successive cutting can weaken basil plants and increase root disease risk such as Pythium in aquaponic systems.
Multi-harvest stress can make nutrient deficiencies visible by about the fourth harvest, with final survival reported around 84.7 percent after harvest cycles.
Downy mildew risk increases when leaf wetness lasts at least 4 hours and night humidity exceeds 95 percent for at least 7.5 hours.
Basil downy mildew pathogen pressure is strongest within about 53 to 77 F, with an optimum around 68 F.

aquaponics_context.notes: Use as aquaponics operating benchmark, not as plant-only optimum.

crop_cycle_context.yield_anchor_basis: harvested cut mass per harvest (kg/m2), basil cut at about 15 cm height and allowed to regrow; fresh weight implied but not stated
crop_cycle_context.harvest_survival_context: Batch final survival about 84.7 percent after four harvests; staggered survival fell to about 64 percent at some harvests due to Pythium. Culled or unmarketable mass is not quantified.

context.system: UVI commercial-scale coupled DWC raft, 214 m2 grow area
context.location: St. Croix, US Virgin Islands, 18 N, outdoor, tropical
context.water_temperature_c_context: about 24 C winter/spring to 29 C summer

crop_cycle_context.density_note: Authors observed that a higher density could be used in raft culture; not tested.
source_basis: Rakocy, Shultz, Bailey, Thoman 2004, Acta Horticulturae 648:63-69, Aquaponic production of tilapia and basil: comparing a batch and staggered cropping system
Rakocy, Bailey, Shultz, Thoman, ISTA6, Update on tilapia and vegetable production in the UVI aquaponic system

anchor_reference_conditions.basis: pH is the batch-trial mean (Rakocy et al. 2004, Table 2). Temperatures are the midpoint of the reported 24 to 29 C water range; air temperature is not reported and is set equal to water temperature as a stated assumption.
anchor_reference_conditions.use: Simulation calibration only: the plant score at these conditions is treated as 100 percent of the yield anchor.

approval.scope: UVI basil crop-cycle values from Rakocy et al. 2004 and ISTA6

evidence.notes: Structured basil Layer 1 corroboration report synthesized from Tier 1 and Tier 2 sources.

yield_response_model.evidence_policy: Trusted Source Map and Source Trust Policy for Aquaponics Layer 1; reliability fields per AGENTS.md 6A
yield_response_model.equation_text: daily_cut_gain_per_plant = anchor_rate x plant_score x nitrate_score x density_factor x light_factor; density_factor = min(1, (density / anchor_density)^(b - 1)); b = 0 above the anchor (closed canopy: kg/m2 does not rise with density), open-canopy b = 0.394 kept for sensitivity; light_factor from DLI points (1.0 when DLI is not given)

exponent_choice.rule: Established, cut-and-regrow basil at or above the UVI anchor density is treated as a closed canopy: yield per m2 is set by light, not plant count, so b = 0 (per-plant mass falls as 1/density). The Ciriello 2021 exponent (0.394, baby-leaf densities 159 to 317 plants/m2) is kept as the open-canopy sensitivity case.
exponent_choice.reason: The UVI anchor plants are already large (2.0 kg/m2 / 8 plants/m2 = 250 g per plant per 28-day cut, our arithmetic), so the canopy is closed at 8 plants/m2. Two independent raft trials at 20 to 23 plants/m2 report per-m2 cut yields below the UVI anchor, not above it: Modarelli et al. 2023 (Plants 12:1355; 20 plants/m2, about 32 to 44 g per plant per cut, about 0.65 to 0.89 kg/m2 per cut, our arithmetic; Naples, under 75 percent shade net) and Corrado et al. 2020 (Agronomy 10:830; 23 plants/m2, two cuts, per-m2 values in figures only). Light differs between these sites, so this is consistency, not a measured density response.
exponent_choice.context_split: Walters and Currey 2015 (DFT, 11 to 100 plants/m2, single harvest three weeks after transplant) found per-m2 yield rising with density and per-plant mass nearly unchanged: young, open canopies, b near 1. That is a different context (single harvest of small plants) and is not applied to established cut-and-regrow crops.

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: Peer-reviewed trials, but none is a density series for established cut basil; the rule is a modelling choice backed by consistency.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: No basil density trial on cut-and-regrow crops between 8 and 40 plants/m2 was found; two raft trials at 20 to 23 plants/m2 are consistent with no per-m2 gain; the Savidov 2005 validation point (31.8 plants/m2) also matches, but it is a validation case, not a source for the rule.

density_response.derivation: Ciriello et al. 2021 Table 1, floating raft: 4.81 kg/m2 at 317 plants/m2 vs 3.66 kg/m2 at 159 plants/m2; b = ln(4.81/3.66)/ln(317/159) = 0.394 (our arithmetic).
density_response.source: Ciriello, Formisano, El-Nakhel, Corrado, Pannico, De Pascale and Rouphael 2021, Frontiers in Plant Science 12:671026
assumptions: The power law fitted at 159 to 317 plants/m2 is extrapolated down to 8 to 32 plants/m2.
Below the UVI anchor density no per-plant gain is credited (cap 1.0); no evidence either way.

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Direction corroborated by Walters and Currey 2015 (DFT, 11 to 100 plants/m2: more plants raise kg/m2, per-plant mass falls slightly); magnitude single source; baby-leaf densities far from UVI's 8 plants/m2.

light_response.derivation: Dou et al. 2018: shoot fresh weight +54.2, +78.6 and +77.9 percent at DLI 12.9, 16.5 and 17.8 vs 9.3 mol/m2/d; normalised to the 16.5 plateau (1.786): 9.3 -> 0.560, 12.9 -> 0.863. DLI 5.5 point: Walters, Tarr and Lopez 2023 fresh-mass model at 23 C gives about 6 g at DLI 5.5 vs 31 g at 13.2, ratio 0.19 applied to the 13.2 factor (0.874) -> 0.166. 0 at DLI 0 and straight lines between points are assumed.

sources.ref: Dou, Niu, Gu and Masabni 2018, HortScience 53(4):496-503 (abstract)
Walters, Tarr and Lopez 2023, PLoS ONE 18(11):e0294905, Table 2 model

light_response.anchor_note: UVI (St Croix, outdoor, tropics) is assumed at or above the plateau (tropical monthly DLI about 20 to 40, Tier 3), so the UVI anchor is unchanged by construction. No measured UVI DLI was found.

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: Peer-reviewed university trials (Texas A&M, Michigan State).
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Direction corroborated by four sources (Dou 2018, Walters 2023, Litvin and Currey 2017, Walters and Currey 2015); Dou read from the abstract only; cultivars and setups differ; low-DLI point mixes two studies.

notes: 2026-11-26: the Knaus 2018 validation now uses DLI 4.3 to 7.2 mol/m2/d (derived from the paper's daytime PAR, separately reported night PAR and Rostock day length); the earlier 12.7 reading treated daytime PAR as a 24 h mean, which the paper's separate night PAR rules out.

gaps: No basil density trial on cut-and-regrow crops between 8 and 40 plants/m2 with absolute yields.
Light and temperature interact (Walters 2023); only light is modelled here.
First cycle after transplant is grown at the regrowth rate of established plants (no establishment lag modelled).
